comments.text: There is heterozygosity for the H63D mutation. This genotype carries only a very slight increased relative risk of hereditary haemochromatosis.

Patients with hereditary haemochromatosis usually have a serum transferrin saturation greater than 50% and an elevated ferritin. Approximately 90% of people with symptoms of hereditary haemochromatosis are homozygous for the C282Y mutation, while approximately 2% of affected individuals are compound heterozygotes for both the C282Y and H63D mutations.

Those individuals who are heterozygous for only the C282Y mutation account for approximately 1% of people with symptoms of hereditary haemochromatosis, while those who are homozygous for the H63D mutation only rarely develop the condition. Approximately 8-10% of people with the symptoms of haemochromatosis do not exhibit either of these genetic abnormalities.
